title_original: Bertrand Bonnefoy : Lagan mon amour, my love, mo ghrá

blocks.text: A traditional Irish song, “My Lagan Love” has the River Lagan singing a lullaby, where a lily sways in the breeze. Legend adds the Leannán sí, a muse who enchants those she loves. What if this French photographer had fallen under her spell? This tribute would then be nothing less than the expression of an enchanting melancholy, on the threshold of another world. A place where carefree eternal youth plays the harp with white, black and evanescence.

“I really like your work. Perhaps because I know its personal story, yours, a story that connects me to the strange and romantic atmosphere that emanates from it. It confirms my understanding of photography.”
Once upon a time, there was a river that never reveals who she is.

Lagan, My Love, My Love, Mo Ghrá is the story of this river in Northern Ireland. A photographer followed its course from the moorlands where it rises to Belfast, where it disappears into the sea. The journey unfolds in four movements: the source, the hinterland, the towpath, and the city of Belfast.

What Bertrand Bonnefoy seeks in the landscape is that which eludes us. A single plane of sharp focus cuts through the visible, while the world all around it dissolves. His photographs inhabit that threshold where the visible recedes, until all that remains is white, black and evanescence.

For Bertrand Bonnefoy, who signs his work BBY, photography is first and foremost a moment of stillness: he pauses with the instant, allowing time for the world to reveal its strangeness. His black-and-white photography is humanist, attentive to the things that pass by.

Bertrand Bonnefoy : Lagan mon amour, my love, mo ghrá Foreword by Glenn Patterson. Bilingual French / English edition.
